s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, and histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells, similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Left facial asymmetry observed during crying and MRI showed a mass at the left cerebellopontine angle

shortlist.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed a mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, and histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed a mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, and patient presented with profound hearing loss in the left ear

raw.rationale: The patient's left facial asymmetry during crying, enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, and histopathological examination revealing a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity and biphasic pattern are consistent with a facial nerve hemangioma.

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: While hemangioma is a type of vascular lesion, the specific location and involvement of the facial nerve and cranial nerve make facial nerve hemangioma a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: The histopathological examination did not reveal features typical of lymphangioma, such as lymphatic endothelium and lack of erythrocytes.

rejected.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The histopathological examination did not reveal features typical of schwannoma, such as Antoni A and Antoni B patterns and S-100 positivity in tumor cells.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and the presence of a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity are not consistent with vestibular schwannoma, which typically occurs in adults and has a different histological appearance.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: The imaging and histopathological findings are not consistent with lymphangioma, which typically appears as a multicystic lesion with lymphatic endothelium.
